import re

def parse_duration(text: str) -> float:
    """
    Convert an ISO 8601 duration string (weeks or days+time) to seconds.
    Accepts only uppercase letters; weeks alone, or days with optional time part.
    Raises ValueError on invalid format or unsupported units.
    """
    # Regular expression for supported formats:
    #   P[n]W
    #   P[n]D[optional time part]
    # Time part: T[n]H[n]M[n]S
    # Only the last component may contain a decimal separator ('.' or ',').
    # All numbers are non-negative integers; decimal part is optional.
    #
    # The regex captures each component separately. We use named groups for clarity.
    pattern = re.compile(
        r"""
        ^P
        (?:
            (?P<weeks>\d+)[W]                                       # weeks only
            |
            (?P<days>\d+)[D]
            (?:
                T
                (?:
                    (?P<hours>\d+)[H]
                    (?P<minutes>\d+)[M]
                    (?P<seconds>\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)[S]
                |
                    (?P<hours_only>\d+)[H]
                    (?P<minutes_only>\d+)[M]
                |
                    (?P<hours_only>\d+)[H]
                    (?P<seconds_only>\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)[S]
                |
                    (?P<minutes_only>\d+)[M]
                    (?P<seconds_only>\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)[S]
                |
                    (?P<hours_only>\d+)[H]
                |
                    (?P<minutes_only>\d+)[M]
                |
                    (?P<seconds_only>\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)[S]
                |
                    (?P<hours>\d+)[H]
                |
                    (?P<minutes>\d+)[M]
                |
                    (?P<seconds>\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)[S]
            )?
        )
        $
        """,
        re.VERBOSE
    )

    m = pattern.match(text)
    if not m:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid ISO 8601 duration: {text!r}")

    # Helper to convert matched string to float, handling ',' as decimal separator
    def to_float(val: str | None) -> float:
        if val is None:
            return 0.0
        return float(val.replace(',', '.'))

    # Compute total seconds
    total = 0.0
    if m.group('weeks'):
        total += int(m.group('weeks')) * 7 * 86400
    else:
        # days
        if m.group('days'):
            total += int(m.group('days')) * 86400
        # hours
        if m.group('hours'):
            total += to_float(m.group('hours')) * 3600
        elif m.group('hours_only'):
            total += int(m.group('hours_only')) * 3600
        # minutes
        if m.group('minutes'):
            total += to_float(m.group('minutes')) * 60
        elif m.group('minutes_only'):
            total += int(m.group('minutes_only')) * 60
        # seconds
        if m.group('seconds'):
            total += to_float(m.group('seconds'))
        elif m.group('seconds_only'):
            total += to_float(m.group('seconds_only'))

    # Ensure at least one component was present
    if total == 0.0:
        raise ValueError(f"No duration components found in {text!r}")

    return total
